PREVENTIVE CARE

Prevention is a programme, not a single product.

Consistent routines make animal-health plans more useful. Build around the environment, the animals and the people responsible for daily care.

IN THIS GUIDE

Map the main risksAgree the daily routinePlan veterinary reviewUse the right care pathway
All resources
01

Map the main risks

Review how animals enter the premises, where they mix, how feed and water are supplied and what changes seasonally. Identify who notices early signs and who contacts the veterinarian. Risk assessment is most useful when it produces actions that staff can actually carry out.

02

Agree the daily routine

Define practical expectations for cleaning, observation, feed and water checks, and recording concerns. Use a consistent handover between shifts or carers. A short reliable record is more valuable than an elaborate form that nobody completes.

03

Plan veterinary review

A preventive programme should be revisited when animals, facilities, management or disease risks change. Vaccination, parasite monitoring and nutritional decisions should reflect the relevant species and local conditions. Monitor outcomes and revise the plan with the attending veterinarian.

04

Use the right care pathway

Flock biosecurity, herd parasite management and companion-animal preventive visits address different needs. Explore the care guides for context, then use the exact locally authorised product documentation for any medicine decision.
